$comment: What a link points at. Guessing from the extension gets pictures right and everything else wrong — a filehost URL is `/f/abc123` with no extension at all — so the server's Content-Type wins where anybody has asked for it. Shared by tests/shared/attachment.test.ts and the Android SharedCorpusTest.
$kinds: `page` is the honest answer for "not known yet" as well as for a real web page: both are resolved by fetching, and both end up either described from their Open Graph tags or offered as a file.

kinds.name: and by what the server says about it
a server that says so wins over an extension that disagrees
an APK from a filehost, which has no extension to go on
a page, which is the thing with Open Graph tags in it
and XHTML is a page too
a parameterised content type still reads as its type
nothing known and no extension is a link like any other
nor is a path that only looks like it has one
an unknown extension is not assumed to be a file

$names: What to call it on the card: the last path segment, unescaped, without the query.

names.name: the query is not part of the name
a trailing slash leaves the segment before it
nothing but a host is the host
a stray percent is a name, not an error

$sizes: Powers of 1024 under the names everybody writes, which is what every file manager and chat client does. Null where the server did not say, so a card leaves the line out rather than printing a confident zero.
